title: Quebec Picks a Party That Wants to Leave Canada
summary:
Quebec is a province in Canada. On Monday, voters there held an election. The Parti Québécois, or PQ, is expected to lead a minority government. That means it won the most seats, but not more than half, so it needs help from other parties.

The PQ wants Quebec to become independent from the rest of Canada. It has promised a public vote, called a referendum, on that idea. The PQ has not led Quebec since 2014.

Its leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, will become Quebec's premier. That job is a bit like a U.S. governor. He promised to be "the premier of everyone in Quebec." He has said a referendum would come only after President Donald Trump leaves office.

It is not clear how a referendum could happen, because the other parties are against independence.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated the new leader.
why_it_matters: Quebec is a close neighbor of the United States, and its choice could change how Canada works together as one country.
